name: pgbuf_timed_sleep_error_handling () -- a page latch waiter that gave up (latch timeout or interrupt) leaves the BCB wait queue and, from the front, hands the READ latch to the READ waiters behind it; when it returns, waiter_exists must equal 'a READ or WRITE waiter is left on the queue' (rule #028 form). develop (bb71348d6) leaves the flag set on every exit, so a READ-latched page keeps blocking non-holder READ requests (and the lock-free READ path) until the holder unlatches -- CBRD-28163. Plus R1: the grant loop adds a reader's fix count before it re-checks the reader under its entry lock, so a reader that gave up in between leaves its count on the BCB (develop same, outside CBRD-28163)
fakes: Real: pgbuf_timed_sleep_error_handling () (called through hooks.cpp's unit_tseh (), same TU) and all it calls in page_buffer.c: PGBUF_BCB_LOCK (pthread_mutex_lock -- pgbuf_Monitor_locks is false), get_impl / compare_exchange on the atomic latch, pgbuf_is_exist_blocked_reader_writer () (head's end check), pgbuf_wakeup () (STATIC_INLINE: resume_status = THREAD_PGBUF_RESUMED, pthread_cond_signal () of the zeroed wakeup_cond, thread_unlock_entry ()). pgbuf_wakeup () is not a seam: unitseam's --seam prefixes `__attribute__ ((weak))` to `STATIC_INLINE int` and reports it applied, but GCC 8.5 warns 'inline function declared weak', drops the attribute and inlines the always_inline body (checked on a copy of the shape: no symbol is emitted) -- a fake would never run. Who is woken is read from resume_status and from the entry lock calls instead. Fakes: cubthread::entry::lock () / unlock () = thread_entry.cpp:397-407 (pthread_mutex_lock / unlock of th_entry_lock) plus a lock / unlock count per entry; in R1 alone the lock () of one READ waiter also sets its request_latch_mode to PGBUF_NO_LATCH -- what that waiter's own pgbuf_timed_sleep () does when it gives up (page_buffer.c cae32d077 :8005 interrupt, :8035 timeout) between the grant loop's unlocked read of the request (:7903) and the loop's thread_lock_entry () (:7914). Inputs as the caller makes them: the giving-up thread's request_latch_mode is PGBUF_NO_LATCH at the call (:8005 / :8035); the call is made without the BCB mutex and returns NO_ERROR holding it (the caller unlocks, :8010 / er_set_return) -- the test checks both and unlocks. A blocked thread carries pgbuf_block_bcb ()'s request (:7733-7734) and resume_status THREAD_PGBUF_SUSPENDED (:7991). The BCB is READ latched by one other thread (fcnt 1) with waiter_exists set. BCB and thread entries are calloc'd (zeroed pthread mutex / cond = the default ones on Linux), never constructed. The contract's right side is computed in test.cpp from the queue, not with the TU's pgbuf_is_exist_blocked_reader_writer ().
